**Surat al-Kawthar (The Abundance)**

Meccan, and its verses are three.

﴿Indeed, We have given you (al-Kawthar).﴾ It is recited as "أنْطَيْناكَ" (*anṭaynāka*, "We have given you"), a variant reading.

﴿al-Kawthar﴾ means: abundant, great good, from the honour of prophethood (*nubuwwah*), which encompasses the good of both abodes and general leadership, which entails the happiness of this world and of religion. It is *fawʿal* (فَوَعْلٌ) on the pattern of abundance (*al-kathrah*). It is said that it is a river in Paradise. The Prophet ﷺ is reported to have recited it and said: "Do you know what al-Kawthar is? It is a river in Paradise which my Lord promised me, in which there is much good." It is related in its description that it is sweeter than honey, whiter than milk, colder than snow, and softer than butter; its banks are of emerald, and its vessels of silver, as many as the stars of the sky. It is related: whoever drinks from it will never thirst. The first to come to it will be the poor emigrants (*fuqarāʾ al-muhājirīn*), those with dirty clothes and disheveled hair, who do not marry women of luxury, and for whom the doors of the well-guarded houses are not opened, one of whom dies while his need stirs in his chest; if he were to swear by God, He would fulfil it for him.

It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may God be pleased with him and his father, that he interpreted al-Kawthar as abundant good. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said to him: "People say it is a river in Paradise." He said: "It is part of the abundant good." It is also said: it is a basin (*ḥawḍ*) in Paradise. It is also said: it is he (the Prophet) and his descendants and his followers, or the scholars of his community, or the Qur'an, which contains the good of this world and religion.

The fa' in His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord﴾ marks the consequence of what follows it from what precedes it. Allah's bestowal upon him, peace be upon him, of the bounty mentioned, which He has not given and will not give to anyone else among the worlds, makes him deserving of the commanded act to the fullest degree. That is: persist in prayer to your Lord, who has poured upon you this magnificent blessing, to which no other blessing is comparable, sincerely for His sake, unlike those who are heedless of it and show off in it, in fulfilment of the rights of thanking Him. For prayer comprises all the kinds of gratitude. ﴿And sacrifice﴾ the camels, which are the choicest of the wealth of the Arabs, in His name, and give charity to the needy, unlike those who turn them away and withhold the ma'un (small kindnesses and necessities) from them. It is narrated from Atiyyah that it refers to the Fajr prayer at Jam' (Muzdalifah) and the sacrifice at Mina. It was also said that it refers to the Eid prayer and the sacrifice. It was also said that it refers to prayer in general, and that the nahr (sacrifice) is placing the right hand upon the left. It was also said that it is raising one's hands to one's chest (nahr) during the takbir. This is what is related from the Prophet (ﷺ), and from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "Face the qiblah with your chest." This is also the view of al-Farra', al-Kalbi and Abu al-Ahwas.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 108, verse 3:

﴿Indeed, your hater﴾ means: your enemy, whoever he may be.

﴿He is the one cut off﴾ who has no posterity (ʿaqib), since no offspring or good remembrance will remain of him. As for you, your descendants, your good reputation, and the traces of your virtue will remain until the Day of Resurrection, and in the Hereafter you will have what cannot be contained within description. It has also been said that it was revealed concerning al-ʿAs ibn Wail. Whichever is the case, there is no doubt about the generality of the ruling.

From the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surah al-Kawthar, Allah the Exalted will give him to drink from every river in Paradise, and he will be recorded as having ten good deeds for every sacrifice that the servants offered on the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-nahr)."
